To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CTGF expression is induced in non-ischemia myocardium in response to MI and (2) CTGF expression in myocardial tissue is induced by the AT1 receptor in response to Ang II and that (3) CTGF is synthesized by cardiac fibroblats.
myocardial induction of CTGF is a novel mechanism of Ang II-induced cardiac remodeling and that CTGF is an effector of AT1 receptor-mediated fibroblast activation and fibrosis in the heart.
the pathophysiologic role of Ang II in the development of HF is mediated, in part, via the induction of myocardium-specific expression of the growth factor CTGF in cardiac fibroblats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel mediators of myocardial remodeling.
the identification and characterization of novel mediators of myocardial remodeling.
the role of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) in the pathogenesis of heart failure (HF).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study demonstrates that myocardium from rats with HF due to MI is characterized by the expression of CTGF.
the induction of CTGF mRNA is a myocardial response to the development of HF in rats with MI.
CTGF is an important mediator of the myocardial response to the Ang II in HF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pathophysiologic mechanism of myocardial remodeling involves the induction of a novel myocardial effector molecule, CTGF, in non-ischemically injured myocardium, which is regulated by the AT1 receptor and which is synthesized by cardiac fibroblastic cells.
the induction of myocardium-specific CTGF mRNA and CTGF protein is an early, sustained, and specific response of myocardial tissue to the pathophysiologic stress of HF.
CTGF is an important mediator of cardiac fibrosis and cardiac fibroblast proliferation induced by Ang II.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CTGF may represent a novel therapeutic target in the treatment of HF.
CTGF is an important effector of myocardial fibroblast activation by the renin-angiotensin system in heart failure.
myocardial fibroblast activation is a key mechanism in the pathogenesis of myocardial remodeling.
